1.description: Bald eagles perched along rivers and coastlines, fishing in cold waters and scavenging salmon carcasses
1.childFriendlyNote: A huge bird with a bright white head sits in a tall tree, watching the water like a king on a throne

1.description: Anna's hummingbirds staying through winter in coastal BC, visiting garden feeders and early flowers
1.childFriendlyNote: A tiny jewel-coloured bird zooms to a feeder and hovers like magic. Its throat flashes pink in the sun!

1.description: Varied thrush singing its haunting single-note whistle from mossy forest canopy in mild coastal rain
1.childFriendlyNote: A beautiful orange-and-grey bird sings one long spooky note from deep in the rainy forest

1.description: Sword ferns stay lush green all winter on the damp forest floor, fronds arching outward like fountains
1.childFriendlyNote: Giant green feathers spread across the forest floor. Run your finger along one and feel the bumpy pattern underneath

1.description: Mosses at their lushest in winter rains, coating tree trunks, branches, and rocks in vivid green velvet
1.childFriendlyNote: Everything wears a thick green fur coat. Press your palm on the moss and feel how soft and squishy it is!

1.description: Towering Douglas fir trees stand evergreen through winter, their bark deeply furrowed and fragrant
1.childFriendlyNote: Tip your head way, way back. These giant trees go up so high they tickle the clouds!

2.description: Bald eagles fishing along rivers and coast, often seen perched on snags overlooking water
2.childFriendlyNote: A huge bird with a bright white head sits in a tall tree, watching the water like a king on a throne

2.description: Anna's hummingbirds singing their scratchy buzzing song from treetops even in January rain
2.childFriendlyNote: Even in the rain, a tiny hummingbird sits on a branch and sings a squeaky, buzzy little song

2.description: Varied thrush foraging on the ground in gardens and parks, flipping leaves to find insects
2.childFriendlyNote: A beautiful orange-and-grey bird hops across wet leaves, flicking them aside to find a snack

2.description: Banana slugs active on wet forest trails, bright yellow bodies gliding over mossy logs
2.childFriendlyNote: A slimy yellow creature slides slowly across a log. It looks like a banana with tiny antennae!

2.description: Western red cedar stands fragrant in the rain, its drooping branches and shreddy bark distinctive
2.childFriendlyNote: Crush a tiny leaf between your fingers and sniff. It smells like a wooden treasure chest!

2.description: Tiny Pacific wrens singing their astonishingly long trilling song from root tangles and fallen logs
2.childFriendlyNote: The tiniest brown bird sings the longest, bubbliest song. It sounds like a tiny waterfall of notes!

3.description: Bald eagles beginning courtship, pairs performing dramatic sky dances and talon-locking aerial displays
3.childFriendlyNote: Two huge eagles grab each other's feet in the sky and spin round and round: it's their way of saying I love you!

3.description: Male Anna's hummingbirds performing spectacular dive displays, climbing high then plummeting with a loud chirp
3.childFriendlyNote: A hummingbird zooms way up high then dives straight down like a tiny rocket (chirp!) at the bottom

3.description: Snowdrops blooming in coastal gardens and parks, white bells nodding in January rain
3.childFriendlyNote: Tiny white bells hang their heads shyly in the rain. They're the bravest flowers, blooming in the cold!

3.description: Varied thrush singing haunting single-note whistles from the misty canopy
3.childFriendlyNote: Stop and listen in the foggy forest. One long, ghostly whistle floats through the trees

3.description: Mosses at peak lushness in the winter rains, entire tree trunks draped in thick green velvet
3.childFriendlyNote: The whole forest looks like it's wrapped in a soft green blanket. Everything is fuzzy and bright!

3.description: Steller's jays calling loudly from conifers, their dark blue plumage and tall crest unmistakable
3.childFriendlyNote: A dark blue bird with a spiky crown yells "shack shack shack" from a tree, so loud and bossy!

4.description: Eagle pairs refurbishing massive stick nests, adding fresh branches and moss
4.childFriendlyNote: Two eagles carry big sticks to their nest: it's so huge, you could lie down inside it!

4.description: Crocuses emerging in parks and gardens, purple and yellow cups opening on sunny days
4.childFriendlyNote: Little purple and yellow cups pop up through the grass like tiny presents from underground

4.description: Anna's hummingbirds visiting winter-flowering shrubs, their gorgets flashing magenta in low sun
4.childFriendlyNote: Watch the hummingbird's throat. It changes from dull grey to blazing pink when it turns its head!

4.description: Banana slugs gliding across wet trails after rain, leaving silvery slime tracks on logs
4.childFriendlyNote: Follow the sparkly silver trail on a log. At the end you'll find a big yellow slug leaving its glittery path!

4.description: Great blue herons stalking shorelines and streams, standing motionless before striking at fish
4.childFriendlyNote: A tall grey bird stands perfectly still like a statue, then (splash) it grabs a fish with its long beak!

4.description: Witch hazel blooming with spidery yellow flowers on bare branches, sweet fragrance in winter gardens
4.childFriendlyNote: Wiggly yellow ribbons burst from bare branches. Lean in and sniff the sweet, magical smell!

5.description: Western skunk cabbage beginning to push bright yellow spathes through wet ground in bogs and stream edges
5.childFriendlyNote: Bright yellow hoods poke up from the mud, but hold your nose, because they smell like a skunk!

5.description: Crocuses in full bloom across parks, bees visiting the purple and gold flowers on warm afternoons
5.childFriendlyNote: A whole carpet of purple and yellow flowers opens wide to catch the sun. Spring is knocking!

5.description: Eagles incubating eggs in their massive nests, one parent always on guard while the other fishes
5.childFriendlyNote: The eagle sits on its huge nest keeping eggs warm. The nest is bigger than your bed!

5.description: Flocks of dark-eyed juncos foraging on the ground, flashing white outer tail feathers when they fly
5.childFriendlyNote: Little grey birds hop around pecking at seeds, then flash white stripes on their tails when they fly away!

5.description: Great blue herons returning to colonial nesting rookeries, repairing stick nests in tall trees
5.childFriendlyNote: Lots of herons building nests in the same big tree. They squawk at each other like noisy neighbours!

5.description: Pacific wrens singing their extraordinary bubbly trill from root balls and fallen logs in damp forest
5.childFriendlyNote: The tiniest bird you've ever seen sings the longest song: a magical waterfall of bubbly notes!

6.description: Skunk cabbage spathes fully open in wetlands, bright yellow beacons in the February forest
6.childFriendlyNote: Glowing yellow hoods stand in the swamp like lanterns. They even make their own heat to melt the snow!

6.description: Snowdrops at peak bloom in coastal gardens, nodding white bells in drifts
6.childFriendlyNote: Hundreds of tiny white bells nod their heads together, a whole fairy garden in the park!

6.description: Nuthatches creeping headfirst down tree trunks, giving nasal "yank-yank" calls from the conifers
6.childFriendlyNote: A little bird walks down the tree trunk upside-down. It honks like a tiny toy trumpet!

6.description: First daffodil shoots pushing up in gardens and parks, green spears rising from winter soil
6.childFriendlyNote: Green swords are pushing up through the dirt. Soon they'll unfurl into golden trumpet flowers!

6.description: Great blue herons nesting in rookeries, loud croaking calls as pairs display and build
6.childFriendlyNote: The tall herons stretch their necks, clack their beaks, and croak to each other at their big nest tree

6.description: Native beaked hazelnut catkins dangling from bare branches, releasing clouds of pollen on dry days
6.childFriendlyNote: Long fuzzy caterpillar-shaped things dangle from branches. Tap one and golden dust puffs into the air!

7.description: Skunk cabbage generating heat to melt surrounding snow, one of the first wildflowers of the year
7.childFriendlyNote: This amazing plant makes its own heat like a warm-blooded animal. It melts a circle of snow around itself!

7.description: Crocuses fading in gardens as early daffodils take over the show
7.childFriendlyNote: The little crocus cups are closing up for the year, but look: golden daffodils are taking their turn!

7.description: Red alder catkins elongating and releasing pollen, one of the first native trees to bloom
7.childFriendlyNote: Long dangly catkins hang from the alders like tiny brown sausages. They shed golden dust in the breeze

7.description: First daffodils opening in coastal gardens, golden trumpets brightening grey February days
7.childFriendlyNote: The first golden daffodils open their trumpets. It's like the ground is playing a fanfare for spring!

7.description: Spotted towhees scratching loudly in leaf litter with both feet, making a racket among the bushes
7.childFriendlyNote: Something is kicking up all the dead leaves. It's a fancy black-and-orange bird doing a backwards dance!

7.description: Hazelnut catkins at peak, tiny red female flowers also visible if you look closely on the twigs
7.childFriendlyNote: Look really closely at the twigs. See the teensy red starbursts? Those are the girl flowers hiding beside the big dangling catkins!

8.description: Daffodils blooming across Vancouver parks and gardens, golden drifts under bare deciduous trees
8.childFriendlyNote: Fields of golden trumpets sway in the breeze. Lean down and sniff their sweet, fresh smell

8.description: Cherry plum trees covered in early white or pink blossoms, a preview of the cherry blossom season ahead
8.childFriendlyNote: Some trees can't wait for spring. They burst into pink flowers while everything else is still bare!

8.description: First Pacific tree frogs beginning to call from wetlands on mild evenings, the classic "ribbit" sound
8.childFriendlyNote: Listen near a pond at dusk, "ribbit! ribbit!". That's a teeny frog no bigger than your thumb!

8.description: Red-flowering currant buds swelling on bare stems, getting ready to burst into drooping pink clusters
8.childFriendlyNote: Fat pink buds are getting ready to pop open. This native bush will soon be covered in candy-pink flowers!

8.description: Song sparrows beginning their spring singing from fence posts and bramble patches, varied musical phrases
8.childFriendlyNote: A stripy brown bird perches on a fence and sings a cheerful bouncy song over and over

8.description: Skunk cabbage leaves beginning to unfurl alongside the bright yellow spathes in boggy areas
8.childFriendlyNote: Giant green leaves start to unroll beside the yellow hoods. They'll grow as big as elephant ears!

9.description: Pacific tree frogs calling in chorus from ponds and ditches, the loudest sound in the evening wetlands
9.childFriendlyNote: Hundreds of tiny frogs singing together, ribbit ribbit ribbit, so loud you can hear them from the road!

9.description: Red-flowering currant bursting into bloom, drooping clusters of deep pink flowers attracting early bumblebees
9.childFriendlyNote: Bunches of candy-pink flowers dangle from bare branches. Bees are buzzing around them already!

9.description: Early-blooming ornamental cherry trees starting to flower in Vancouver, pale pink clouds appearing on streets
9.childFriendlyNote: Whole trees are turning into pink candy floss. The cherry blossoms are starting their magical show!

9.description: Daffodils at peak bloom, masses of gold in parks, gardens, and roadsides
9.childFriendlyNote: Everywhere you look: gold, gold, gold! The daffodils have turned the whole world sunny

9.description: First rufous hummingbirds arriving from Mexico, fiery orange males buzzing into coastal gardens
9.childFriendlyNote: A brand new hummingbird arrives. This one is bright copper-orange and flew all the way from Mexico!

9.description: Steller's jays getting vocal as spring approaches, mimicking hawk calls to scare other birds from feeders
9.childFriendlyNote: The blue jay with the punk-rock crest pretends to be a hawk (keeer!) and all the little birds fly away. Sneaky!

10.description: Cherry blossoms beginning to peak across Vancouver, streets and parks transformed into tunnels of pink and white
10.childFriendlyNote: Whole streets turn into pink fairy tunnels. Petals fall like warm snow and land in your hair!

10.description: Pacific tree frogs in full chorus at wetlands, calling intensely from pond edges and flooded ditches
10.childFriendlyNote: The pond is so noisy with frog songs you can't hear your friend talking, ribbit ribbit everywhere!

10.description: Red-flowering currant at peak bloom, hanging clusters of rose-pink flowers buzzing with bees and visited by hummingbirds
10.childFriendlyNote: Pink flower bunches drip from every branch. Hummingbirds zip from cluster to cluster like they're at a buffet!

10.description: Rufous hummingbirds arriving in numbers, males chasing each other and performing dramatic dive displays
10.childFriendlyNote: Fiery orange hummingbirds chase each other around the garden. They're tiny but so fierce and angry!

10.description: First white trillium flowers appearing on the forest floor, three pristine petals above three broad leaves
10.childFriendlyNote: Everything comes in threes (three white petals, three green leaves), like a forest fairy's favourite number!

10.description: Song sparrows in full voice, each male singing his unique variation from a prominent perch
10.childFriendlyNote: Every song sparrow makes up his own song. Listen to two different ones and hear how their tunes are different!

11.description: Cherry blossom season at full peak in Vancouver, over 40,000 trees creating cascades of pink across the city
11.childFriendlyNote: The whole city is draped in pink. Petals rain down like confetti and pile up on the sidewalks!

11.description: Tree frogs laying eggs in ponds, gelatinous masses of eggs attached to submerged plants
11.childFriendlyNote: Look in the pond for wobbly blobs of jelly with tiny black dots. Each one will become a baby frog!

11.description: Salmonberry bushes flowering with bright pink blooms in forest understory and stream edges
11.childFriendlyNote: Hot pink flowers pop open on thorny bushes by the stream. Later they'll turn into yummy orange berries!

11.description: Trillium flowers carpeting the forest floor, fresh white blooms that will slowly turn pink as they age
11.childFriendlyNote: White three-petalled flowers dot the forest like fallen stars. Watch over the weeks as they slowly blush pink!

11.description: Rufous hummingbirds aggressively defending flowering currant patches, buzzing intruders away
11.childFriendlyNote: This tiny copper bird thinks the whole bush belongs to him. He chases away birds twice his size!

11.description: Queen bumble bees emerging from hibernation, visiting early spring flowers and searching for nest sites
11.childFriendlyNote: A big fuzzy bee with a yellow face bumbles along. She's a queen looking for the perfect spot for her nest!

12.description: Peak cherry blossom continues with mid-season varieties, petals drifting like snow on breezy days
12.childFriendlyNote: Stand under a cherry tree when the wind blows. It's a pink snowstorm and the petals tickle your face!

12.description: Salmonberry in full bloom along streams and forest trails, bright magenta flowers attracting hummingbirds
12.childFriendlyNote: Bright pink flowers cover the bushes along every path. Hummingbirds dart between them like little rockets!

12.description: Trillium at peak bloom on the forest floor, some early flowers already blushing pink with age
12.childFriendlyNote: Can you spot the white ones and the pink ones? The pink trilliums are the older, wiser flowers!

12.description: First violet-green swallows returning from the south, swooping over ponds and fields catching insects
12.childFriendlyNote: Shiny green-and-white birds zoom through the sky scooping up bugs. They just arrived from their winter holiday!

12.description: Indian plum (osoberry) blooming with drooping clusters of small white flowers, one of the first native shrubs to leaf out
12.childFriendlyNote: Dangling white flower bells hang from branches that already have fresh green leaves. Smell them, they're like almonds!

12.description: Bumble bee queens visiting flowering currant, salmonberry, and garden flowers, buzzing loudly
12.childFriendlyNote: Fat fuzzy bees crawl deep inside pink flowers, their bums poking out as they slurp up nectar

13.description: Late cherry blossom varieties blooming, petals carpeting sidewalks and floating in puddles
13.childFriendlyNote: Pink petals float in every puddle like tiny boats. Scoop some up and let them drift from your hand!

13.description: Salmonberry flowers fading as small green berries begin to form on the bushes
13.childFriendlyNote: The pink flowers are dropping off and leaving behind tiny green bumpy balls. Future berries are growing!

13.description: Bigleaf maples bursting into leaf and flower simultaneously, huge drooping yellow-green flower clusters
13.childFriendlyNote: The biggest maple trees wake up all at once, fresh green leaves and dangling flower tassels at the same time!

13.description: Rufous hummingbirds nesting, females building tiny lichen-covered cup nests on branches
13.childFriendlyNote: The mama hummingbird builds a nest the size of a walnut shell, using spider silk to glue it together!

13.description: Pacific bleeding heart emerging on the forest floor, delicate pink heart-shaped flowers on arching stems
13.childFriendlyNote: Tiny pink hearts dangle from a curved stem. The forest is growing valentines!

13.description: American robins singing their cheerful "cheerily cheer-up" song from dawn, pulling worms from lawns
13.childFriendlyNote: The orange-bellied robin tilts its head, listening, then tugs a wiggly worm right out of the grass, pop!

14.description: Final wave of cherry blossom with double-flowered Kanzan varieties, deeper pink and more ruffled blooms
14.childFriendlyNote: The last cherry trees bloom with extra-fluffy double flowers. They look like popcorn dipped in pink paint!

14.description: Bigleaf maple fully leafing out, enormous leaves unfurling that can be wider than a dinner plate
14.childFriendlyNote: Hold a bigleaf maple leaf next to your face. It might be bigger than your whole head!

14.description: Bleeding heart in full bloom on the forest floor, delicate fernlike foliage with arching sprays of pink hearts
14.childFriendlyNote: Little pink hearts hang in a row like a necklace. The forest floor is decorated with love!

14.description: Barn swallows arriving from Central America, swooping low over fields and water with forked tails
14.childFriendlyNote: Birds with long forked tails zoom and swoop over the field like tiny acrobats. They never stop moving!

14.description: Trillium flowers aging from white to deep rose-pink, the forest floor scattered with both colours
14.childFriendlyNote: The white trilliums are blushing deeper and deeper pink. They change colour as they get older!

14.description: Robins singing loudly at dawn and dusk, building mud-cup nests in garden trees and under eaves
14.childFriendlyNote: The robin wakes you up singing before the sun! Look for its nest made of mud and grass in a tree fork

15.description: First camas lily shoots pushing up in meadows and oak savannahs, getting ready for their spectacular blue-purple bloom
15.childFriendlyNote: Green spikes are rising from the ground. Soon this whole meadow will turn purple-blue like an ocean!

15.description: Bigleaf maples fully leafed out, helicopter seeds (samaras) beginning to develop in dangling clusters
15.childFriendlyNote: The giant maple leaves make a green roof over the path. Look up and see sunlight glowing through them!

15.description: Ospreys returning to their platform nests on tall poles and dead trees near water, carrying fish
15.childFriendlyNote: A big brown-and-white hawk hovers over the water, then splashes in feet-first and flies up with a fish!

15.description: Barn swallows swooping over fields and ponds, their metallic blue backs flashing in spring sunlight
15.childFriendlyNote: Shiny blue-and-orange birds swoop past your head so close you can hear the wind in their feathers, whoosh!

15.description: Red-flowering currant finishing bloom, small green berries forming where the flowers were
15.childFriendlyNote: The pink flowers are finished but look: tiny green balls are growing where each flower used to be!

15.description: Violet-green swallows nesting in tree cavities and nest boxes, males' iridescent backs flashing green and purple
15.childFriendlyNote: These swallows live in little holes in trees. Watch them zoom out, grab a bug, and zoom right back in!

16.description: Camas beginning to bloom in meadows around Victoria and the Gulf Islands, blue-purple spires rising
16.childFriendlyNote: Blue-purple star flowers start opening on tall green stalks, a whole meadow of tiny blue stars!

16.description: Bleeding heart at peak in shady forest, lush ferny leaves with dancing pink hearts above
16.childFriendlyNote: Rows of tiny pink hearts sway in the forest breeze like a valentine garland strung between the ferns

16.description: Rufous hummingbirds nesting and defending flower territories fiercely, visiting salmonberry and currant
16.childFriendlyNote: The feisty orange hummingbird guards every flower. It chatters angrily if another bird comes close!

16.description: Garry oaks leafing out on Vancouver Island, their twisted branches framing meadows of emerging wildflowers
16.childFriendlyNote: The gnarly, twisty oak trees finally put on their green clothes. They're always the last ones to dress up!

16.description: Tree frogs still calling from ponds but chorus fading as breeding season winds down
16.childFriendlyNote: The pond frogs are getting quieter now. Their singing season is slowing down, but you can still hear a few

16.description: Orange-crowned warblers arriving and singing their rapid trilling song from shrubs and low trees
16.childFriendlyNote: A little yellow-green bird buzzes a fast trill from inside a bush. It just arrived from far away Mexico!

17.description: Camas meadows reaching full bloom, entire fields turned brilliant blue-purple on Vancouver Island and Gulf Islands
17.childFriendlyNote: The meadow looks like a blue-purple ocean. First Nations people tended these beautiful flowers for thousands of years!

17.description: First salmonberries ripening to golden-orange and deep red, the earliest wild berry of the season
17.childFriendlyNote: The first berries of summer! Salmonberries come in orange and red. They look like tiny bumpy jewels

17.description: Ospreys settled on nests, spectacular fishing dives with talons extended into lakes and rivers
17.childFriendlyNote: The fishing hawk circles, circles, then folds its wings and crashes into the water. Up it comes with a fish in its claws!

17.description: First native rhododendrons beginning to bloom in coastal forests, large trusses of pink flowers
17.childFriendlyNote: Big round bunches of pink flowers open up on dark green bushes. Each bunch is like a bouquet!

17.description: Swainson's thrush arriving and beginning its ethereal upward-spiralling song at dusk in deep forest
17.childFriendlyNote: At sunset in the forest, a bird sings a magical song that spirals up, up, up like a musical staircase!

17.description: Bumble bee colonies growing, workers foraging busily on rhododendron, salmonberry, and garden flowers
17.childFriendlyNote: Busy fuzzy bees buzz from flower to flower, their back legs loaded with bright yellow pollen saddlebags!

18.description: Camas at peak bloom, meadows a sea of blue-purple, culturally significant to Coast Salish and other First Nations
18.childFriendlyNote: Stand in the middle of the blue meadow and pretend you're swimming. The flower ocean stretches everywhere!

18.description: Native and garden rhododendrons blooming profusely, huge flower trusses in shades of pink, purple, and white
18.childFriendlyNote: Giant balls of flowers in every colour burst from dark green bushes. It's like the garden is having a party!

18.description: Barn swallows building mud nests under eaves and bridges, swooping low over fields for insects
18.childFriendlyNote: The swallows carry tiny balls of mud in their beaks and stick them together to build a cup-shaped nest!

18.description: Swainson's thrush in full song at dawn and dusk, upward-spiralling flute-like phrases from the canopy
18.childFriendlyNote: Close your eyes at sunset and listen. A bird plays a flute that goes up and up like climbing a rainbow!

18.description: Salmonberries ripening along trails, golden-orange and ruby-red drupelets soft and juicy
18.childFriendlyNote: Pick a ripe salmonberry and it falls apart in your fingers. Pop it in your mouth for a sweet juicy treat!

18.description: Bigleaf maples in full canopy, trunks covered in licorice fern and moss, helicopter seeds dangling
18.childFriendlyNote: Look at the mossy maple trunk. Tiny ferns grow right on the bark! It's a garden growing on a tree!

19.description: Camas still blooming strongly in meadows, seed pods beginning to form on earliest flowers
19.childFriendlyNote: Some camas flowers are turning into green seed pods while others are still bright purple. Nature recycles!

19.description: First Nootka rose buds swelling in hedgerows and forest edges, getting ready to open
19.childFriendlyNote: Fat pink buds on thorny stems are getting ready to pop open into beautiful wild roses!

19.description: Ospreys incubating eggs on platform nests, one parent always standing guard while the other hunts fish
19.childFriendlyNote: The osprey sits patiently on its big stick nest keeping eggs warm, while its partner brings home fresh fish!

19.description: Red-breasted sapsuckers drilling neat rows of holes in tree bark and lapping up the flowing sap
19.childFriendlyNote: A red-headed woodpecker drills tiny holes in neat rows and licks up the sweet tree juice like a lollipop!

19.description: Foxglove rosettes growing vigorously in forest clearings and roadsides, tall flower spikes beginning to push up
19.childFriendlyNote: Tall green towers are shooting up. Soon they'll be covered in purple bell flowers that fit over your fingertip!

19.description: Swainson's thrush singing their upward-spiralling song from deep forest at dawn and dusk
19.childFriendlyNote: The forest flute bird plays its magical rising song. It sounds like the music is climbing up a ladder!

20.description: Nootka roses blooming in hedgerows and along trails, large single pink flowers with golden centres
20.childFriendlyNote: Wild pink roses open along the path. Lean in and smell one, it's the sweetest perfume in the forest!

20.description: Foxglove spikes starting to bloom from the bottom up, purple bell-shaped flowers with spotted throats
20.childFriendlyNote: A tall tower of purple bells opens from the bottom up. Peek inside one and see the spotted pattern!

20.description: Native rhododendrons at peak in coastal forests, massive pink flower clusters glowing in the shade
20.childFriendlyNote: In the shade of the big trees, huge round flower bouquets glow pink like lanterns in the forest!

20.description: Black bears active in coastal forests, grazing on fresh grass, skunk cabbage leaves, and emerging berries
20.childFriendlyNote: Bears are out munching on green grass and plants after their long winter nap. They're very hungry!

20.description: Bald eagle chicks hatching in massive nests, fluffy grey down visible when parents come and go
20.childFriendlyNote: Baby eagles are fuzzy grey fluffballs sitting in a nest the size of a bathtub. Both parents bring them fish!

20.description: Cedar waxwings arriving in sleek flocks, silky plumage with waxy red wing tips, feeding on insects
20.childFriendlyNote: A flock of fancy birds with black masks and smooth hair-like feathers. They look like tiny superheroes!

21.description: Nootka roses in full bloom along hedgerows and forest edges, their sweet scent filling the air
21.childFriendlyNote: Every hedge is dotted with sweet-smelling pink roses. Bees crawl inside and come out dusted in golden pollen!

21.description: Foxglove at peak, tall purple spires standing in forest clearings and along roadsides
21.childFriendlyNote: Tall towers of purple bells reach up to your waist. Bumble bees climb right inside each bell for nectar!

21.description: Invasive Himalayan blackberry covering waste ground with white and pink flowers, visited heavily by bees
21.childFriendlyNote: Thorny blackberry bushes burst into white flowers. This summer they'll turn into the yummiest berries!

21.description: Swainson's thrush singing at peak intensity, the soundtrack of Pacific Northwest summer evenings
21.childFriendlyNote: As the sun sets, the forest fills with the most beautiful rising flute song. It's pure magic!

21.description: Tadpoles developing in ponds, tiny dark wrigglers with feathery external gills
21.childFriendlyNote: Look in the pond. Hundreds of tiny dark tadpoles wriggle around like beans with tails!

21.description: First dragonflies emerging near ponds, hovering and darting over the water surface hunting mosquitoes
21.childFriendlyNote: A helicopter bug with see-through wings hovers over the pond. It can fly forward, backward, and sideways!

22.description: Wild roses still blooming beautifully, petals beginning to drop on the warmest days
22.childFriendlyNote: Pink rose petals fall softly to the ground. Collect them gently and smell the sweetness in your palm

22.description: Foxglove at peak height, some spires over 150cm tall, new flowers opening at the top while lower ones set seed
22.childFriendlyNote: The foxgloves are taller than you! Look how flowers bloom at the top while seeds grow at the bottom

22.description: Blackberry in full flower, white and pink blossoms covering every hedgerow and waste ground
22.childFriendlyNote: So many white flowers on the blackberry bushes. Each one is a promise of a juicy berry later!

22.description: Resident and transient orca pods beginning to be spotted in the Salish Sea and Georgia Strait
22.childFriendlyNote: Look out to sea. You might spot a big black fin slicing through the water! That's an orca, the ocean's wolf!

22.description: Cedar waxwings passing berries beak to beak while perched in a row, their famous sharing behaviour
22.childFriendlyNote: These polite birds sit in a row and pass a berry down the line, beak to beak. They share their food!

22.description: Tadpoles growing rapidly in warm ponds, some developing tiny hind leg buds
22.childFriendlyNote: The tadpoles are growing back legs! Tiny bumps poke out near their tails. They're becoming frogs!

23.description: Blackberry flowers fading and tiny green fruits beginning to form in clusters
23.childFriendlyNote: The white flowers are dropping petals and leaving behind hard green bumpy berries. They need more sun to ripen!

23.description: Wild roses fading, the first small green rose hips forming where flowers were
23.childFriendlyNote: The pink petals have fallen off and left behind a little green ball. That's a baby rose hip growing!

23.description: Orca pods more frequently seen in the Salish Sea, following salmon runs through the straits
23.childFriendlyNote: Black-and-white orcas swim together in family groups. Baby orcas stay right next to their mums!

23.description: Multiple dragonfly species active around ponds and streams, iridescent wings glinting in June sun
23.childFriendlyNote: Dragonflies zoom around the pond like tiny helicopters. Their wings sparkle in the sunshine like glass!

23.description: Eagle chicks growing rapidly, standing in the nest and flapping wings, beginning to look like real eagles
23.childFriendlyNote: Baby eagles stand up in their big nest and flap their wings like they're practicing, almost ready to fly!

23.description: Ocean spray bursting into plumes of tiny creamy-white flowers, drooping clusters decorating forest edges
23.childFriendlyNote: Creamy white flower sprays droop from the branches like frozen waterfalls. They smell like honey!

24.description: Ocean spray at peak bloom, masses of creamy flower plumes along roadsides and forest openings
24.childFriendlyNote: The bushes are draped in creamy-white flower curtains that smell sweet and drift in the warm breeze!

24.description: Orcas actively hunting in the straits, dramatic breaching and spy-hopping visible from shore
24.childFriendlyNote: An orca leaps right out of the water (splash!) twisting in the air before crashing back down!

24.description: Foxglove still blooming at the top of tall spires, lower flowers setting seed in brown capsules
24.childFriendlyNote: The foxglove tower still has purple bells opening at the very tip-top, even as seeds rattle below!

24.description: Dragonflies patrolling territories along pond edges, darting and hovering with incredible agility
24.childFriendlyNote: Watch a dragonfly guard its favourite spot on the pond. It chases away every other dragonfly that comes close!

24.description: Thimbleberry bushes covered in large white flowers in forest clearings, big maple-like leaves
24.childFriendlyNote: Papery white flowers bloom above huge fuzzy leaves. Feel how soft the leaves are, like green velvet!

24.description: Harbour seals pupping on rocky islets and beaches, spotted pups resting beside their mothers
24.childFriendlyNote: Baby seals with spotted coats lie on the rocks with their mums. They have the biggest, roundest eyes!

25.description: Green blackberries developing in clusters, hard and sour, still weeks away from ripening
25.childFriendlyNote: The berries are still green and hard as marbles. Don't eat them yet, they need more sunshine to sweeten up!

25.description: Ocean spray flowers fading from creamy white to tan, the dried plumes persisting on branches
25.childFriendlyNote: The white flower sprays are drying to golden-brown and rattling in the breeze like paper streamers

25.description: Orca pods actively foraging in Georgia Strait and around the San Juan Islands, tall dorsal fins visible
25.childFriendlyNote: A whole family of orcas swims past. Count the tall black fins cutting through the glittering water!

25.description: Osprey chicks visible in nests, parents making frequent fishing trips to feed hungry young
25.childFriendlyNote: Fuzzy osprey chicks peek over the edge of their nest and squeak for more fish, so hungry all the time!

25.description: First thimbleberries beginning to ripen, soft red berries shaped like little thimbles
25.childFriendlyNote: Red velvety berries shaped like tiny hats. Pick one gently and pop it on your fingertip like a thimble!

25.description: Young eagles nearly fully feathered, branching out along nest tree limbs and making short test flights
25.childFriendlyNote: The young eagle hops to the edge of the nest, spreads its wings, and takes a big brave leap. It can fly!

26.description: First blackberries turning from green to red, still not yet ripe, the first dark ones still a couple weeks away
26.childFriendlyNote: The berries are blushing red now. Getting closer! But wait for them to turn shiny black before you eat one

26.description: Thimbleberries ripening along forest trails, soft dome-shaped red berries that collapse when picked
26.childFriendlyNote: These soft red berries squish flat in your hand. Eat them right away because they don't keep! So delicious!

26.description: Orcas highly active in the straits, both resident salmon-eating pods and transient seal-hunting pods
26.childFriendlyNote: Orcas blast out misty breaths (pssshh!) and you can see the spray hang in the air before they dive deep

26.description: Dragonflies abundant along ponds and lakeshores, hawking insects in warm summer air
26.childFriendlyNote: Dragonflies are everywhere! Watch them catch tiny bugs right out of the air, better than any fighter jet!

26.description: Black bears browsing on berries, grasses, and insects, sometimes seen in suburban areas near forests
26.childFriendlyNote: Bears love berries as much as you do! They use their long tongues to scoop them off the bushes

26.description: Western tiger swallowtail butterflies gliding through gardens and along streams, bright yellow with black stripes
26.childFriendlyNote: A big yellow butterfly with black tiger stripes floats through the garden. It has little tail streamers too!

27.description: First blackberries turning dark and beginning to ripen, the earliest ones sweet on south-facing brambles
27.childFriendlyNote: The first shiny black berries are ready! Pull one gently. If it falls off easily, pop it in your mouth. So sweet!

27.description: Thimbleberries at peak ripeness in forest shade, soft red berries falling apart in the hand
27.childFriendlyNote: Thimbleberries are so ripe they practically jump into your hand. Eat them on the trail, they taste like summer!

27.description: Oregon grape berries turning dusty blue-purple, tart clusters hanging beneath holly-like leaves
27.childFriendlyNote: Purple-blue berries covered in dusty coating hang in bunches. They look like tiny grapes but taste super sour!

27.description: Humpback whales increasingly common in BC waters, lunge-feeding on herring and krill near shore
27.childFriendlyNote: A whale as big as a school bus blasts water from its blowhole, whoosh, you can see it from far away!

27.description: Tiger swallowtails visiting garden flowers and mud puddles, gathering minerals from damp earth
27.childFriendlyNote: Big yellow butterflies gather at a mud puddle to sip. It's a butterfly party at the water cooler!

27.description: Cedar waxwings nesting late, feeding on abundant summer berries and catching insects for their young
27.childFriendlyNote: The masked berry-birds are busy feeding their babies. They give high-pitched whistles as they fly by!

28.description: Blackberries ripening fast in the July heat, dark glossy drupelets in sunny hedgerows
28.childFriendlyNote: Blackberry season! Your fingers turn purple picking the fat juicy berries. Save some for a pie!

28.description: Humpback whales feeding regularly in BC waters, sometimes breaching spectacularly near shore
28.childFriendlyNote: A giant whale leaps out of the ocean and crashes back down, the biggest belly flop in the world!

28.description: Oregon grape berries at peak, dusty blue-purple clusters attracting birds and bears
28.childFriendlyNote: Bunches of dusty purple berries dangle below spiky leaves. Birds gobble them up like candy!

28.description: Peak orca season in the Salish Sea, whale-watching boats following pods through the islands
28.childFriendlyNote: The biggest orcas have dorsal fins taller than you. Watch them surface, blow mist, and dive again!

28.description: Dragonflies at peak abundance, darners and skimmers hunting over every pond and lake
28.childFriendlyNote: Giant blue dragonflies zoom past like tiny fighter jets, catching mosquitoes before you can even blink!

28.description: Osprey chicks nearly fledged, young birds exercising wings on nest platform before first flights
28.childFriendlyNote: Young ospreys flap their wings on the nest like they're doing jumping jacks, almost time for their first flight!

29.description: Peak blackberry season, bushes heavy with dark ripe fruit in every hedgerow and vacant lot
29.childFriendlyNote: So many berries your bucket overflows! The biggest, fattest ones hide in the middle where it's hardest to reach

29.description: Humpbacks bubble-net feeding in groups, creating curtains of bubbles to trap schools of herring
29.childFriendlyNote: Whales blow a ring of bubbles underwater to trap fish, then lunge up through the middle with mouths wide open!

29.description: Late summer dragonflies including meadowhawks beginning to appear in reddish tones
29.childFriendlyNote: New red dragonflies are joining the blue ones. The pond is like a colourful air show!

29.description: Fireweed at peak bloom in clearings and roadsides, tall magenta spires lighting up the landscape
29.childFriendlyNote: Tall pink-purple towers line the road. They say when fireweed blooms reach the top, summer is almost over!

29.description: Black bears gorging on berries in preparation for winter, eating up to 20,000 berries per day
29.childFriendlyNote: Bears eat berries all day long to get fat for winter. Imagine eating 20,000 berries in one day!

29.description: Young eagles learning to fish, making clumsy attempts while parents soar overhead
29.childFriendlyNote: Teenage eagles practice fishing. They splash and miss a lot, but keep trying until they catch one!

30.description: Blackberries still at peak, the warmest hedgerows producing the sweetest fruit in the dry summer heat
30.childFriendlyNote: The berries warmed by the sun taste the sweetest. Eat the warm black ones right off the bush. Yum!

30.description: Fireweed blooming higher up the stalk, lower flowers setting fluffy white seed heads
30.childFriendlyNote: Pink flowers at the top, fluffy white seeds at the bottom. The plant is half flower, half cotton candy!

30.description: Humpback whales abundant in coastal BC, tail flukes visible as they dive deep for fish
30.childFriendlyNote: The whale lifts its huge tail straight up before a deep dive. Every tail has a different pattern, like a fingerprint!

30.description: Oregon grape berries fully ripe, dark blue-purple with a dusty bloom, popular with birds
30.childFriendlyNote: The blue berries are being eaten fast by hungry birds. Rub the dusty coating off to see the dark purple underneath!

30.description: Barn swallow families with fledglings, young birds perching in rows on wires being fed by parents
30.childFriendlyNote: Baby swallows sit on a wire in a row, mouths wide open, as mum and dad zoom back and forth with bugs!

30.description: Tiger swallowtails still gliding through gardens, their numbers beginning to thin as summer wanes
30.childFriendlyNote: The big yellow-and-black butterflies are still floating around. Enjoy them now before they disappear!

31.description: Blackberry season winding down, the best fruit picked over but still good berries on north-facing slopes
31.childFriendlyNote: Hunt for the last hidden berries in the shady spots. The treasure hunt is half the fun!

31.description: Fireweed flowers reaching the top of the stalk, the old saying goes: when fireweed tops out, summer ends in six weeks
31.childFriendlyNote: The pink flowers reached the tippy top of the plant. The old timers say that means summer is counting down!

31.description: Humpbacks continuing to feed in rich coastal waters, sometimes seen very close to shore
31.childFriendlyNote: A whale surfaces so close to the beach you can hear it breathe (pfffhhh!) like a giant snoring!

31.description: Red huckleberries ripe in the forest understory, translucent red jewels on bright green bushes growing from nurse logs
31.childFriendlyNote: Tiny red berries glow like rubies in the forest shade. They grow right on top of old rotten logs!

31.description: Young great blue herons fledged from rookeries, gangly juveniles learning to fish on their own
31.childFriendlyNote: Clumsy young herons wade in the shallows, stabbing at fish and missing. They're still learning!

31.description: Red meadowhawk dragonflies common along paths and fences, perching with wings forward in warm sun
31.childFriendlyNote: Little red dragonflies sit on fence posts warming themselves in the sunshine. They're so bright they glow!

32.description: Late blackberries still available in shaded spots, some berries drying on the vine in the August heat
32.childFriendlyNote: The last berries of summer are hiding in the shade. They might be small but they're extra sweet!

32.description: Fireweed setting seed, fluffy white plumes drifting through the air like summer snowflakes
32.childFriendlyNote: White fluff fills the air like snow in summer! Each tiny parachute carries a seed to a new home

32.description: Red huckleberries still available in the forest, tart and flavourful, favoured by grouse and bears
32.childFriendlyNote: Pop a huckleberry in your mouth (zap!) it's tart and sweet and makes your tongue tingle!

32.description: Humpback whales still feeding actively in BC waters, preparing for their migration south
32.childFriendlyNote: The whales are eating as much as they can. They're fattening up for a very long swim south!

32.description: Eagles soaring over late-summer landscape, juvenile eagles dark brown without the white head markings
32.childFriendlyNote: Young eagles are all dark brown. It takes them four years to grow the famous white head and tail!

32.description: Yellowjackets increasingly bold at picnics and around garbage, late-summer colonies at peak size
32.childFriendlyNote: Buzzy yellow-and-black wasps want your sandwich! Stay calm and they'll usually fly away on their own

33.description: Fireweed pods splitting open, releasing clouds of silky white seeds into the warm August wind
33.childFriendlyNote: Thousands of tiny white parachutes float through the sunny air. Catch one and make a wish!

33.description: Blackberry season ending, remaining fruit drying on the canes, birds finishing off the last berries
33.childFriendlyNote: The last wrinkly berries are left for the birds. Blackberry season is saying goodbye for this year

33.description: Early chinook salmon beginning their journey upstream, the first scouts of the great salmon runs to come
33.childFriendlyNote: The first big salmon are swimming up the rivers. They've crossed the whole Pacific Ocean to come home!

33.description: Red huckleberries fading, the last berries being gobbled up by thrushes and bears
33.childFriendlyNote: The huckleberry bushes are almost bare. The birds and bears beat you to the last ones!

33.description: Great blue herons fishing in shallows and on rocky shores, standing perfectly still in golden late-summer light
33.childFriendlyNote: The heron stands like a grey statue in the golden evening light (then zap!) a fish dinner in one snap!

33.description: Large orb-weaving spiders building impressive webs in gardens, dewdrops revealing intricate silk patterns
33.childFriendlyNote: Huge spider webs sparkle with morning dew. Each one is a work of art that took all night to build!

34.description: Chinook salmon swimming upstream in larger numbers, their dark backs visible in shallow riffles
34.childFriendlyNote: Big salmon fight their way up the river. You can see their backs poking out in the shallow parts!

34.description: Wild rose hips turning orange-red on hedgerow bushes, plump and full of vitamin C
34.childFriendlyNote: The roses have turned into little red balls. Birds love them, and people can make jam from them too!

34.description: Large cross spiders at peak, spectacular orb webs strung between bushes, heavy with morning dew
34.childFriendlyNote: Each web is a perfect wheel of silk threads. The fat spider sits in the middle waiting for a fly to get stuck!

34.description: Barn swallows gathering on wires in large groups, getting ready for their long migration south
34.childFriendlyNote: Hundreds of swallows line up on the wires like notes on a music sheet. They're planning their big trip south!

34.description: Eagles beginning to gather near salmon streams, anticipating the autumn runs
34.childFriendlyNote: Eagles are showing up along the rivers. They know the salmon are coming and they want front-row seats!

34.description: Yellowjackets at peak boldness, desperate for sugar as their colony begins to break down
34.childFriendlyNote: The wasps are extra pesky right now because they're really hungry. Cover your juice and stay still!

35.description: Coho salmon beginning to enter coastal rivers, their silver bodies turning darker as they push upstream
35.childFriendlyNote: Silver salmon are arriving from the ocean. Watch them leap up the rapids like fishy superheroes!

35.description: Rose hips turning deep red-orange, standing out brightly against the still-green hedgerows
35.childFriendlyNote: Shiny red-orange balls dot the hedges like Christmas decorations put up early by the plants!

35.description: First Pacific golden chanterelles appearing in coastal forests after late-summer rains
35.childFriendlyNote: Golden trumpet-shaped mushrooms peek through the forest floor. They smell like apricots!

35.description: First hints of yellow appearing on bigleaf maples, the earliest trees showing autumn stress from dry summer
35.childFriendlyNote: Some maple leaves are going yellow at the edges. The trees are getting tired from the long hot summer

35.description: Eagles increasingly common along salmon streams, perching on snags and watching the water intently
35.childFriendlyNote: More and more eagles line up along the river like fans at a game. The salmon feast is about to begin!

35.description: Red meadowhawk dragonflies perching on warm rocks and fence posts in the late-summer sunshine
35.childFriendlyNote: Ruby-red dragonflies bask on sunny rocks. They're soaking up the last warm days before autumn!

36.description: Salmon runs intensifying, chinook, coho, and pink salmon pushing up rivers, bodies changing colour as they near spawning grounds
36.childFriendlyNote: The rivers are full of salmon! Their bodies turn red and green as they swim home to where they were born

36.description: Bigleaf maples beginning to turn golden yellow, the first autumn colour in the Pacific Northwest
36.childFriendlyNote: The giant maple leaves are turning golden like coins. Hold one up to the sun and see it glow!

36.description: Chanterelles emerging in coastal Douglas fir forests, golden funnel shapes pushing through moss and needles
36.childFriendlyNote: Golden trumpet mushrooms push through the mossy forest floor. They smell fruity and wonderful!

36.description: Bald eagles congregating along salmon streams, snatching fish from the shallows and perching in riverside trees
36.childFriendlyNote: Eagles swoop down and grab salmon right out of the river with their huge talons. Splash and they're gone!

36.description: Last barn swallows departing for Central and South America, wires and skies emptying out
36.childFriendlyNote: The swallows are leaving! Wave goodbye. They'll fly all the way to South America and back again next spring

36.description: Spider webs everywhere in September mist, orb weavers at their largest size of the year
36.childFriendlyNote: Walk through the misty garden and you'll see webs everywhere, sparkling with tiny water diamonds!

37.description: Salmon runs at peak intensity, rivers alive with spawning fish, the defining ecological event of the Pacific Northwest
37.childFriendlyNote: So many salmon you could almost walk across the river on their backs! They splash and leap everywhere

37.description: Bigleaf maples turning brilliant gold, enormous leaves fluttering down and carpeting the ground
37.childFriendlyNote: Giant golden leaves float down like dinner plates. Catch one! It might be bigger than your face!

37.description: Chanterelle season building after autumn rains, golden fungi dotting the forest floor under conifers
37.childFriendlyNote: The forest floor is sprinkled with golden treasure. Chanterelle mushrooms smell like peaches and pepper!

37.description: Vine maples turning vivid orange and red in forest understory, one of the most colourful autumn trees
37.childFriendlyNote: Small maple trees in the forest light up in orange and red like little campfires among the green!

37.description: Dozens of eagles gathering at productive salmon streams, perching in trees and feasting
37.childFriendlyNote: Count the eagles, 5, 10, 20, they're everywhere along the river having the biggest fish dinner ever!

37.description: Dark-eyed juncos returning to lowland gardens and parks for winter, flashing white tail feathers
37.childFriendlyNote: The little grey snowbirds are back! Watch for the flash of white feathers when they fly from bush to bush

38.description: Salmon actively spawning, females digging redds in gravel while males fight for position, the air thick with the smell of fish
38.childFriendlyNote: Mama salmon uses her tail to dig a nest in the gravel. She flaps so hard the stones fly! Then she lays her eggs

38.description: Vine maples at peak autumn colour, fiery orange-red against the dark green of conifers
38.childFriendlyNote: The little maples blaze orange and red like torches in the dark green forest, autumn's own campfires!

38.description: Chanterelle mushrooms abundant after September rains, the most prized wild mushroom of the Pacific Northwest
38.childFriendlyNote: Golden chanterelles are popping up everywhere after the rain. They look like little upside-down umbrellas!

38.description: Bigleaf maple leaves falling in golden showers, creating thick rustling carpets along forest trails
38.childFriendlyNote: Crunch crunch! Kick through the golden carpet of giant leaves. They're almost too big to fit in your hand!

38.description: Eagles feasting at salmon streams, sometimes dozens in a single tree, a spectacular autumn gathering
38.childFriendlyNote: One tree has ten eagles in it! They're all waiting their turn to swoop down and grab a salmon

38.description: Varied thrush returning to lowland forests and gardens for winter, their haunting whistle heard again
38.childFriendlyNote: A beautiful orange-and-grey bird whistles one long spooky note from the misty trees. Winter is coming!

39.description: Chum salmon arriving in streams, their bodies developing dramatic green and purple tiger stripes
39.childFriendlyNote: These salmon turn into green-and-purple striped tigers! Their teeth grow into scary fangs for fighting

39.description: Vine maples dropping their colourful leaves, forest floor scattered with orange-red confetti
39.childFriendlyNote: Red and orange leaves drift down from the vine maples like nature's confetti. Scoop up a handful!

39.description: Peak chanterelle season in coastal forests, experienced foragers harvesting baskets of golden fungi
39.childFriendlyNote: The forest floor is a treasure hunt. Golden mushrooms hide under ferns and fallen leaves. Can you spot them?

39.description: Eagle concentrations growing along salmon rivers, the autumn gathering building to its peak
39.childFriendlyNote: The eagle convention gets bigger every day. They come from hundreds of kilometres away for the salmon feast!

39.description: Hedgehog mushrooms appearing alongside chanterelles, creamy-orange caps with tiny teeth underneath instead of gills
39.childFriendlyNote: Flip this mushroom over and feel underneath. Instead of lines it has tiny soft teeth like a hedgehog belly!

39.description: Varied thrush now common in lowland parks and gardens, singing their eerie single-note whistle
39.childFriendlyNote: One long ghostly whistle rings through the rainy garden. The autumn bird is back to sing in the fog!

40.description: Spent salmon dying after spawning, their decaying bodies fertilizing the forest, a circle of life moment
40.childFriendlyNote: The salmon's journey is over. Their bodies feed the trees and baby fish, keeping the circle of life going

40.description: Bigleaf maples nearly bare, huge golden leaves piled deep along trails and in gutters
40.childFriendlyNote: Wade through knee-deep piles of giant golden leaves, swish swish. They crunch and rustle under your feet!

40.description: Chanterelles still fruiting in the damp October forest, season continuing with steady autumn rains
40.childFriendlyNote: The rain keeps the golden mushrooms popping up. The forest floor is a treasure chest that refills itself!

40.description: Huge gatherings of bald eagles along salmon rivers, some streams hosting hundreds of birds
40.childFriendlyNote: Hundreds of eagles in one place! Every tree branch, every rock, every sandbar has an eagle sitting on it!

40.description: Juncos common in gardens and parks, hopping on the ground and flashing white tail feathers
40.childFriendlyNote: Cute grey birds with white flashing tails hop around in the fallen leaves. They're here for winter!

40.description: Banana slugs active again with autumn rains, bright yellow bodies crossing forest trails
40.childFriendlyNote: The banana slugs are back! The rain woke them up. They leave sparkly silver trails across every log

41.description: Chum salmon still spawning in coastal streams, green-and-purple striped bodies fighting in the shallows
41.childFriendlyNote: Stripy green-and-purple salmon still splashing in the creek. They never give up even when they're tired!

41.description: Chanterelles still available but season beginning to slow, the best specimens found in sheltered spots
41.childFriendlyNote: Fewer golden trumpets now. The mushroom treasure hunt is getting harder but the prizes are still there!

41.description: Eagles continuing to feast on salmon, some streams attracting spectacular concentrations
41.childFriendlyNote: Eagles carry big salmon in their claws and fly to a perch to eat. The fish is almost as big as the eagle!

41.description: Oyster mushrooms fruiting in overlapping clusters on dead and dying alder and maple trees
41.childFriendlyNote: Stacked shelves of white mushrooms grow out of a dead tree like little stairs. They smell like the sea!

41.description: Varied thrush common in lowland forests and gardens, their single-note whistle the soundtrack of autumn rain
41.childFriendlyNote: In the rain, one bird sings one note that sounds like the forest itself is humming, so beautiful and sad

41.description: Rose hips deep red and softening with frosts, an important food source for overwintering birds
41.childFriendlyNote: The red rose hips are soft and squishy now. Birds peck them open to eat the seeds inside!

42.description: Salmon carcasses lining stream banks, a dramatic but essential nutrient transfer from ocean to forest
42.childFriendlyNote: The salmon's journey is done. Their bodies become food for eagles, bears, and even the trees!

42.description: Late chanterelles and other woodland fungi still fruiting in the wet October forest
42.childFriendlyNote: The last golden chanterelles hide under wet leaves. You have to look extra carefully to find them now!

42.description: Eagles still concentrated at salmon rivers, some birds beginning to disperse as fish runs wind down
42.childFriendlyNote: The eagles are still at the river buffet. They've been eating fish for weeks and look very well-fed!

42.description: Mosses reviving with autumn rains after summer dormancy, tree trunks and rocks turning vivid green again
42.childFriendlyNote: The rain wakes up the moss! It turns from dry brown to squishy bright green, like magic green paint!

42.description: Oyster mushrooms at peak on dead wood, beautiful overlapping white-to-grey shelves
42.childFriendlyNote: White mushroom shelves stack up the side of a dead tree. They look like stairs for a fairy!

42.description: Juncos in large winter flocks, twittering calls as they forage together through leaf litter
42.childFriendlyNote: A gang of grey birds with white belly flashes hops through the leaves together, chattering away!

43.description: Hedgehog mushrooms at peak in coastal forests, pale orange caps with distinctive tooth-like spines underneath
43.childFriendlyNote: This mushroom has soft tiny teeth under its cap instead of lines, like a friendly hedgehog belly!

43.description: Late chum salmon still entering streams, the last wave of the autumn spawning season
43.childFriendlyNote: The last brave salmon are still swimming upstream. They're the final runners in nature's marathon!

43.description: Moss intensely green and lush after weeks of autumn rain, coating every surface in the forest
43.childFriendlyNote: The whole forest is wrapped in thick green velvet. Press your hand into the moss and feel the squish!

43.description: Eagles dispersing from salmon streams back to coastal territories, still fishing along rivers and shores
43.childFriendlyNote: The eagle party is winding down. The well-fed birds fly home to their favourite trees along the coast

43.description: Varied thrush a constant presence in rainy autumn forests, foraging on the ground and singing from the canopy
43.childFriendlyNote: The orange-bellied bird hops through the wet leaves, stops to listen, then sings one long whispery note

43.description: Banana slugs very active in the wet autumn forest, some individuals as long as a ruler
43.childFriendlyNote: The banana slugs are huge right now. Some are as long as a ruler! They leave shiny silver highways on every log

44.description: Oyster mushrooms still fruiting on dead wood, handling the colder temperatures well
44.childFriendlyNote: White mushroom shelves keep growing on dead trees even as it gets cold. They don't mind the chill!

44.description: Varied thrush singing regularly in lowland forests and gardens, the quintessential sound of BC's wet season
44.childFriendlyNote: One long ringing note floats through the November fog. The varied thrush is the voice of the rainy forest

44.description: Moss at its most luxuriant, entire tree trunks and stumps buried under thick emerald carpets
44.childFriendlyNote: The forest looks like it's been painted in every shade of green. Soft squishy moss covers everything!

44.description: Juncos abundant in winter flocks, their tinkling calls and flashing white tails a constant in gardens
44.childFriendlyNote: The little grey snowbirds are everywhere! They hop-hop-hop on the ground and tinkle like tiny bells

44.description: Salmon carcasses decomposing along stream banks, feeding the forest ecosystem through the winter
44.childFriendlyNote: The salmon gave everything to have their babies. Now their bodies feed the trees and the bugs and the river

44.description: Anna's hummingbirds still active at garden feeders and winter-flowering plants as other hummingbirds have migrated
44.childFriendlyNote: While all the other hummingbirds flew south, Anna's hummingbird stays. It's tough enough for winters here!

45.description: Winter chanterelles (yellowfoot) appearing in damp conifer forests, thin-capped brown-and-yellow fungi
45.childFriendlyNote: Skinny brown-and-yellow mushrooms cluster on the forest floor. They're the cold-weather cousins of chanterelles!

45.description: Varied thrush singing from misty cedars and hemlocks, the haunting whistle echoing through November rain
45.childFriendlyNote: One ghostly whistle hangs in the foggy air, the most magical sound in the whole rainy forest

45.description: Moss spectacularly lush in the November rains, every surface in the forest softened in green
45.childFriendlyNote: The rain makes the moss puff up like a green sponge. Squeeze some gently and watch the water drip out!

45.description: Steller's jays caching acorns and seeds for winter, busy and noisy in forest and garden
45.childFriendlyNote: The crested blue jay stuffs seeds in hiding spots and yells at everyone. It's the noisiest bird in the forest!

45.description: Great blue herons stalking winter shorelines, grey silhouettes in the November mist
45.childFriendlyNote: A tall grey ghost stands in the misty water, perfectly still, patient, waiting for a fish to swim by

45.description: Banana slugs still active in the mild November forest, crossing trails after every rainfall
45.childFriendlyNote: Step carefully on the trail. Big yellow slugs are everywhere after the rain, leaving sparkly paths!

46.description: Winter chanterelles (yellowfoot) at peak in wet conifer forests, growing in large troops among moss
46.childFriendlyNote: Troops of little brown-and-yellow mushrooms march across the mossy forest floor like a tiny army!

46.description: Varied thrush a fixture of the rainy November forest, singing and foraging on the wet ground
46.childFriendlyNote: Rain patters on the leaves, and through it you hear one clear, beautiful note. The forest is singing back

46.description: Bald eagles back on coastal and riverside territories, fishing and scavenging through the dark months
46.childFriendlyNote: The white-headed eagle sits on a bare branch above the grey water, watching for fish with its super-sharp eyes

46.description: Anna's hummingbirds visiting garden feeders and late-blooming flowers, puffing up feathers against the cold
46.childFriendlyNote: The hummingbird puffs up its feathers like a tiny green ball to stay warm. It visits the feeder even in rain!

46.description: Sword ferns lush and green on the forest floor, evergreen fronds catching raindrops
46.childFriendlyNote: The sword ferns stay green all year! Listen to the rain drumming on their big fronds like tiny drums

46.description: Spotted towhees noisily scratching through leaf litter under hedges, rusty flanks flashing
46.childFriendlyNote: Who's making all that scratching noise in the bushes? A black-and-orange bird does a backwards kick-dance in the leaves!

47.description: Winter chanterelles still abundant in wet forests, the season's most reliable late mushroom
47.childFriendlyNote: Even in November the forest gives gifts. Little yellow-stemmed mushrooms cluster everywhere in the moss!

47.description: Oyster mushrooms continuing to fruit on dead wood through late autumn, tolerating cold and wet
47.childFriendlyNote: White mushroom shelves keep growing on old logs even as winter comes. They're the toughest mushrooms around!

47.description: Anna's hummingbirds singing their scratchy courtship song even in November, establishing winter territories
47.childFriendlyNote: Can you believe it? The hummingbird is singing in November rain! It's picking its favourite garden already

47.description: Varied thrush visiting berry bushes and leaf litter in gardens, the orange breast bright against grey skies
47.childFriendlyNote: The orange-bellied bird is a bright spot on a grey day. It hops through the garden like a little sunrise!

47.description: Western red cedars standing strong in winter rain, their drooping branches shedding water beautifully
47.childFriendlyNote: The big cedar tree sheds rain from its droopy branches like a living umbrella. Smell the spicy wood!

47.description: Nuthatches busy at garden feeders and on tree trunks, creeping headfirst down bark with nasal calls
47.childFriendlyNote: A tiny bird walks down the tree trunk upside-down. No other bird does that! It goes "yank yank yank"!

48.description: Winter chanterelles still fruiting in mild coastal forests, the last mushroom hurrah before deep winter
48.childFriendlyNote: The little yellowfoot mushrooms are still poking up through the moss, the very last mushrooms of autumn!

48.description: Bald eagles fishing along the coast and rivers, sometimes gathering at late salmon runs
48.childFriendlyNote: The eagle sits proud on a branch above the grey ocean, its white head the brightest thing in the whole sky

48.description: Moss at peak winter glory, every tree, rock, and stump cushioned in thick emerald green
48.childFriendlyNote: The whole forest is a green wonderland. Every log, every rock, every branch wears a thick mossy coat!

48.description: Varied thrush singing through the darkening days, the eerie whistle more haunting than ever in early winter
48.childFriendlyNote: As the days get short, one beautiful whistle rings through the dark forest. The winter singer is here

48.description: Steller's jays visiting feeders and scavenging boldly, their dark blue plumage vivid against grey skies
48.childFriendlyNote: The bossy blue jay with the spiky crest screams from the feeder: "This is my peanut! Go away!"

48.description: Juncos in busy winter flocks, foraging under feeders and in garden leaf litter
48.childFriendlyNote: A flock of snowbirds bounces under the bird feeder, pecking up all the seeds the bigger birds dropped!

49.description: Bald eagles prominent along rivers and coast, white heads and tails standing out against dark winter skies
49.childFriendlyNote: Even on the greyest day, the eagle's white head shines like a beacon from the top of a tall tree

49.description: Anna's hummingbirds surviving December cold by torpor at night, active at feeders during the day
49.childFriendlyNote: This amazing tiny bird sleeps so deeply in the cold it looks frozen, then wakes up in the morning and buzzes to the feeder!

49.description: Varied thrush singing its winter song from rain-dark conifers, an iconic Pacific Northwest winter sound
49.childFriendlyNote: The forest is dark and dripping. And then one beautiful note rings out, clear as a bell. That's the thrush!

49.description: Sword ferns standing green and proud through December rain, the eternal green of the coastal forest floor
49.childFriendlyNote: While other plants sleep for winter, the sword ferns stay wide awake and bright green. They love the rain!

49.description: Douglas fir trees towering over the winter forest, their distinctive cones with mouse-tail bracts littering the ground
49.childFriendlyNote: Pick up a Douglas fir cone. See the tiny mouse tails sticking out between the scales? Mice hiding in the cone!

49.description: Towhees noisily scratching through winter leaf litter with their trademark two-footed backward hop
49.childFriendlyNote: Scratch scratch scratch. Something's making a huge racket in the leaves! It's just a towhee doing its leaf dance

50.description: Bald eagles fishing and soaring along the December coast, some birds beginning courtship behaviour
50.childFriendlyNote: Two eagles fly side by side over the winter ocean. They're already starting to think about building a nest!

50.description: Anna's hummingbirds singing even in December, males performing dive displays on milder days
50.childFriendlyNote: The hummingbird doesn't care that it's December. It sings a buzzy song and does diving tricks in the winter sunshine!

50.description: Moss at its most intensely green in the December rains, the forest floor a carpet of emerald
50.childFriendlyNote: The greenest green you've ever seen! December moss is so bright it almost seems to glow in the rain

50.description: Varied thrush visiting garden berry bushes and singing from hemlock and cedar branches in winter rain
50.childFriendlyNote: A flash of orange hops onto the berry bush. Then the thrush flies to a tree and sings its winter lullaby

50.description: Western red cedars majestic in winter rain, their drooping sprays of scale-like leaves dripping with moisture
50.childFriendlyNote: Rub a cedar leaf between your fingers. The spicy, woody smell is like opening a treasure chest on a rainy day!

50.description: Great blue herons hunting in winter shallows, hunched against the cold, patient as statues
50.childFriendlyNote: The big grey heron stands perfectly still in the cold water, rain dripping off its beak, so patient!

51.description: Eagles soaring on winter thermals, pairs returning to traditional nesting territories
51.childFriendlyNote: The eagles are going back to their favourite trees. They use the same nest year after year!

51.description: Anna's hummingbirds brave the shortest days, visiting feeders frequently in the limited daylight hours
51.childFriendlyNote: The tiny hummingbird has to eat every 10 minutes to stay alive in winter. What a brave little bird!

51.description: Varied thrush singing through the darkest week of the year, its ethereal whistle the sound of winter solstice
51.childFriendlyNote: On the shortest, darkest day of the year, the thrush still sings. One clear note says everything will be okay

51.description: Sword ferns evergreen and lush on the forest floor, their symmetrical fronds a constant through every season
51.childFriendlyNote: The sword ferns never change. They're the steady, reliable friends of the forest, green through rain, cold, and everything!

51.description: Winter junco flocks foraging actively in garden leaf litter and under feeders in short December days
51.childFriendlyNote: The snowbirds hop and peck all day because winter days are short. They need to eat fast before dark!

51.description: Banana slugs still active in the mild coastal forest, slowing down but not yet dormant
51.childFriendlyNote: Even in December, yellow banana slugs slide along on mild days. They're the slowest winter hikers!

52.description: Bald eagles on winter territories, some pairs already repairing nests for the coming breeding season
52.childFriendlyNote: The eagle pair starts fixing up their huge nest already. They add new sticks while snow falls around them!

52.description: Anna's hummingbirds at garden feeders on the last days of the year, their iridescent gorgets flashing even in low winter light
52.childFriendlyNote: A tiny jewel visits the feeder on the last day of the year, pink throat flashing like a Christmas light!

52.description: Varied thrush singing from rain-soaked conifers as the year ends, the quintessential BC winter sound
52.childFriendlyNote: The year ends with the thrush's beautiful whistle echoing through the misty forest. Goodnight, old year!

52.description: Moss at full winter glory, the coastal rainforest draped in endless shades of green despite the season
52.childFriendlyNote: While the rest of the world looks grey and bare, the mossy forest stays green as ever, nature's winter miracle!

52.description: Steller's jays bright and noisy at garden feeders, caching peanuts and seeds for the lean months ahead
52.childFriendlyNote: The bold blue jay grabs a peanut and flies off to hide it in a secret spot. It remembers hundreds of hiding places!

52.description: Douglas fir standing tall as the year turns, ancient evergreen sentinels of the Pacific Northwest
52.childFriendlyNote: The giant Douglas fir has watched hundreds of years go by. Tip your head back and say happy new year to the tree!
